sections.overview: The Woodlark is a Palearctic lark found in Europe and extending east to Russia.
sections.identification: Compared with the Eurasian Skylark (Alauda arvensis), it is smaller and more compact, with a markedly shorter tail and a pale eyebrow that meets behind the head.
sections.habitat: It favors dry, well-drained open or semi-open ground with short, sparse grass, including heath, pasture and young woodland.
sections.diet: It takes insects and other small invertebrates especially in the warm season, and relies more on seeds in winter.
sections.behavior: Some birds breeding in the UK spend winter on the continent.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground; breeding generally starts earlier in southern populations than farther north, and a pair may raise two broods.
sections.ecology: The Eurasian Skylark is a related lark also covered in this Bestiary, but the Woodlark is smaller, shorter-tailed and more likely to use low perches.
sections.conservation: The consulted French account gives the global IUCN category as Least Concern; this global label does not rule out local declines.
